findings.description: The new positive control is one-sided, and the axis it omits is the one that decides whether Phase 0 override 1 is tested at all. B-4 specifies the control as 'the baseline script at 298c8a6 against case A1' -- a DIRTY case. Its stated purpose is 'so a broken harness announces itself instead of manufacturing nine passes,' but it announces nothing about any harness defect that silently dirties the scratch repo before the run, which is the defect B-4's own `code` bullet says 'matters most' ('turns a clean case dirty, which silently collapses V-1's clean/dirty axis into one column'). With the clean axis collapsed, a guard placed AFTER the clean-tree early exit at :130-133 -- exactly what Phase 0 override 1 forbids, and what the constitution itself calls 'half the incident's cost' -- passes all nine V-1 cases, all three per-detector mutations, V-2, V-3, V-4 and V-5, and passes the positive control too. No clause records the one observation that would expose it: V-1 records `git rev-list --count HEAD` and `git diff --cached --name-only` before each run, but never `git status --porcelain`, so nothing ever confirms that A2/B2/C2/D2 are actually clean. Fix: make the control two-sided -- also run the baseline against A2 and require `==> Nothing to commit. Already in sync.` with no commit created -- and/or have V-1 record pre-run `git status --porcelain` and assert it is empty for the four clean cases.
findings.evidence: Demonstrated end to end. Built a guard identical to a correct one except placed after :133 (sync-defective). Under a correct harness it fails as it should: A2/B2/C2/D2 EXIT=0, so V-1 catches it. Under a harness whose clean cases are silently dirty, all nine V-1 cases pass: A1 EXIT=1 1->1 staged[]; A2 EXIT=1 1->1; B1/B2/C1/C2 EXIT=1 1->1; D1/D2 EXIT=1 1->1; E1 EXIT=1 2->2 staged[c.txt,] unchanged. All three per-detector mutations still flip (delete detached -> A1,A2 EXIT=0 1->2; delete rebase -> B1,B2,C1,C2 EXIT=0 1->2; delete merge -> D1,D2 EXIT=0 1->2), so the mutation step does not save it. V-5 does not save it either: on A2 the log has 1 'Refusing' line and 0 'Nothing to commit' lines, which is exactly what V-5 requires. B-4's control as written passes on the same harness: baseline at 298c8a6, case A1 -> EXIT=0, commits 1->2. Two independent realizations measured, one of which violates no B-4 rule: (a) `code` reachable with $SRC/dot_config/ present -> clean case commits 1->2; (b) $STUBS and $HOME placed INSIDE the scratch repo, which B-4 never forbids -> A2 porcelain is '?? stubs/', baseline on A2 prints '==> Committing 1 file' instead of 'Nothing to commit', and sync-defective on A2 returns EXIT=1 commits 1->1 with '==> Refusing: HEAD is detached'. constitution.md:134 (control), :43 (placement), :60 (pre-run observations), :9 (Phase 0 override 1).

findings.description: The check requires a committed case for the ATTACHED path to exist but never requires a committed case for any BLOCKED state, and the mutation step it relies on for that is vacuous over an empty set. 'Require that the cases covering that detector's state report `not ok`' is satisfied trivially when no such case exists. So a test file containing nothing but the attached case satisfies B-3's check in full, clears D-2's count floor (120 -> 121), and passes every other clause, leaving spec AC 7's detached half with no committed coverage. This is the mirror image of the r1 major that revision 3 was written to close: r1 found the attached half unmapped, and the fix mapped it by name while leaving the blocked half to an existence-blind mutation step. The clause's own text does require both ('The committed cases cover both the blocked states and the attached path'), so text and check diverge -- the exact defect species revision 3's own log names. Partially mitigated by 'Name the case-to-mutation mapping in the verdict,' which would render an empty mapping conspicuous. Fix: mirror the attached sentence -- require at least one committed case per blocked state before the mutation step runs.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:121 (check: 'confirm the committed test file contains at least one case driving the attached, no-operation path' -- no equivalent sentence for the three blocked states; the mutation step's quantifier is over 'the cases covering that detector's state'), against :120 (text: 'cover both the blocked states and the attached path, per spec AC 7'). D-2's only count requirement is `bats --count tests/` > 120 (constitution.md:148); measured `bats --count tests/` = 120 at 298c8a6, so one attached case clears it. spec.md:66.

findings.description: The new notification half instructs the checker to 'confirm from V-1's runs that the stubbed `osascript` was invoked,' but nothing produces that datum for it to read. V-1's per-case record is fixed at three items -- `git rev-list --count HEAD`, `git diff --cached --name-only`, and the exit code -- and says nothing about osascript. B-4 requires the stub to record its invocation, but into an ephemeral scratch dir V-1's checker is never told to preserve or report. And V-1 now insists the nine-case probe is 'the checker's own,' which makes the artifact private to whichever checker holds V-1. A checker assigned V-3 on its own therefore cannot follow the instruction as written, and the natural fallback is the half it CAN do -- read the call site -- which is the same half-checking defect r1 filed against V-3, reproduced one level down. Fix: say explicitly that V-3's checker runs its own nine-case probe under B-4's harness, or add the osascript invocation record to V-1's per-case observations so it appears in V-1's verdict. Note V-2 ('from V-1's nine runs, capture output per case') and V-5 ('from V-1's clean-tree cases') carry the same coupling, but both are phrased as actions the reading checker performs rather than as a lookup against another clause's output.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:78 ('Read the call site and confirm from V-1's runs that the stubbed `osascript` was invoked') against :60 (V-1's per-case record: commit count, staged-path list, exit code -- osascript absent) and :62 ('This probe is the checker's own'). B-4's recording requirement is at :131. The coupling is at least not VACUOUS in the other direction: measured, in a refusal run the only other osascript caller is the template-drift `notify` at dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:97, which is unreachable because B-4 stubs `chezmoi status` to empty output, so 'osascript was invoked' really does imply the refusal notified.

findings.description: One input to the commit sha is still unpinned, and the clause's corrected causal account walks past it. The commit message is built at :142 as `[auto-sync from ${HOST}] $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) - ...`. That `date -u` is wall-clock and GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE do not reach it, so two runs that straddle a UTC midnight get different messages, hence different shas, and the clause forbids normalizing anything but the scratch path. The clause lists 'message' among the sha's inputs and then treats the whole message as content-determined. The window is roughly one second of exposure per day per run pair, so this is a minor, not a repeat of the r1 blocker -- but it is the same shape and deserves a sentence.
findings.evidence: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:142. constitution.md:87 ('A commit's id is a function of its tree, message, author and committer identity and dates, and its parent'). Observed in the measured runs: the commit line reads `[main <sha>] [auto-sync from That-Air] 2026-08-09 - 1 file` while the local date is 2026-08-08, i.e. the runs sit on the far side of a UTC day boundary already.

findings.description: Carried unaddressed from r1, and revision 3's log does not claim to have folded it in (only the probe-delegation minor was). The text pins the guard 'after `cd "$SRC"` at :128 and before the clean-tree early exit at :130-133,' but the check verifies behavior only. The before-:130 half is behaviorally observable through the clean cases; the after-:128 half is not. A guard written with `git -C "$SRC"` above the `cd` satisfies every assertion in the check while violating the letter of the text. Harmless in effect, but a checker asked to enforce the text has no method for half of it.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:43 (text) against :44-64 (check). `cd "$SRC"` confirmed at dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:128; the clean-tree early exit at :130-133. Revision log at constitution.md:37 folds in only the r1 minor about V-1's probe being the checker's own.

findings.description: The deterministic half of the new notification check asks only whether osascript was invoked, not whether it was invoked by `notify_fail`. `notify_fail` at :33-36 delegates to `notify` at :28-31, which is also called on success paths, so the two are distinguishable only by the title argument -- `Dotfiles sync failed` versus anything else. B-4's stub already records the invocation, so recording and asserting the title costs nothing and would make the empirical half discriminate between the helper the clause names and the generic one beside it. As written only the call-site read separates them.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:78 ('confirm ... that the stubbed `osascript` was invoked'); :131 (B-4's stub 'records its invocation', with no requirement on what it records). dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:28-31 (`notify`, `osascript -e "display notification \"$2\" with title \"$1\""`) and :33-36 (`notify_fail` -> `notify "Dotfiles sync failed" "$1"`).

findings.description: The restore instruction is circular as written. Both V-1 and B-3 say to restore between mutations 'with `cp` from the working tree, never `git checkout`.' The mutation has to be applied in place to the working-tree script, because B-3 drives it through `bats tests/<new file>` and the suite resolves the script from the repo path; so 'the working tree' is the mutated file, and cp'ing from it restores nothing. The intended procedure is obviously to take a backup copy first and cp that back, and the stated reason for banning `git checkout` (it would discard the worker's uncommitted work) is sound -- but the backup step is never named, and B-4's own principle is that 'every stub is named rather than assumed.'
findings.evidence: constitution.md:64 ('restoring between each with `cp` from the working tree and never `git checkout`') and :121 ('Restore with `cp` from the working tree, never `git checkout`'). Test files resolve the script from the repo, e.g. tests/doctor.bats:16 `SCRIPT="$SRC/dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-doctor"`, so a mutation must be in place for B-3's bats run to see it.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the r1 blocker is genuinely closed, by measurement rather than by reading the revision log. Pinning GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE through scratch-repo setup makes the merged streams identical across every trial I could produce, well past the flake rate r1 measured; not pinning setup reproduces the flake. The corrected causal account in the clause is also right: the parent commit is made during setup and env vars scoped to the run never reach it.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline at 298c8a6 versus a copy of the working-tree script, two independently built scratch repos, authoritative stub PATH, scratch path normalized with sed, merged stream plus exit code compared. Dates pinned through setup, dirty tree: 30/30 IDENTICAL (10 back-to-back, 3 at a 1.2s gap, 1 at 2s, 1 at 3s, 15 at random gaps 0-2.5s). Setup unpinned, dirty tree: 5 of 8 DIFFER, every difference on the `[main <sha>] [auto-sync from That-Air] 2026-08-09 - 1 file` line and nothing else. Clean tree: IDENTICAL either way (no commit, no sha). constitution.md:87.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the D1/D2 blocker is closed. `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD` makes the two idiomatic merge probes agree, so the case no longer decides the outcome by construction and the merge-detector mutation can no longer report a working detector as dead. The construction is also faithful to reality: a real conflicted merge writes a commit id there, and git itself reports the synthetic state as a merge in progress.
findings.evidence: Measured on a scratch repo. Empty marker (`: > .git/MERGE_HEAD`): `test -f` rc=0, `git rev-parse --verify -q MERGE_HEAD` rc=1 -- they disagree. Required form (`git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD`): `test -f` rc=0, `git rev-parse --verify -q MERGE_HEAD` rc=0, `git rev-parse -q --verify` rc=0 -- they agree; `git status` prints 'All conflicts fixed but you are still merging.'; `git status --porcelain` stays empty so the clean cases stay clean. constitution.md:58.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, and specifically NOT self-defeating: the authoritative PATH leaves the harness fully runnable on this machine. `git` resolves from /usr/bin, not Homebrew, so excluding /opt/homebrew/bin costs the harness nothing, and every other tool the script reaches for is in /usr/bin or /bin. All five commands the clause requires to be absent live outside those two directories, so the required PATH really does make them absent. The positive control as the clause now specifies it commits, and under the r1 defect it does not -- so the control catches the exact defect it was added for.
findings.evidence: which -a git -> /usr/bin/git only (git version 2.39.3, Apple Git-146). hostname /bin, sort /usr/bin, wc /usr/bin, tr /usr/bin, date /bin, grep /usr/bin, tee /usr/bin, mkdir /bin, sed /usr/bin, tail /usr/bin, osascript /usr/bin. Required-absent tools: code and brew and jq -> /opt/homebrew/bin; claude-plugins-capture and claude-settings-normalize -> ~/.local/bin. None in /usr/bin or /bin. Positive control run as specified (baseline at 298c8a6, `export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"`, case A1): EXIT=0, commits 1->2, reached :130 and committed. Same control under the r1 prepending form `PATH="$STUBS:$PATH"`: EXIT=1, commits 1->1, staged unchanged -- all three V-1 assertions satisfied with no guard present, i.e. the control flips from pass to fail exactly where it should. constitution.md:133-134; tests/apps.bats:73 confirmed as `export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"`; tests/doctor.bats:62 confirmed as `export PATH="$STUBS:$PATH"`.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the corrected `code` rationale is factually right in both halves, which is what r1 said the old one was not. The failed redirect does not abort under `set -e` -- bash prints the error, the phase prints its success line anyway, and execution continues to the next phase. And the real hazard the clause now names is real: with $SRC/dot_config/ present, the phase writes vscode-extensions.txt into the scratch repo and a case built as clean commits instead.
findings.evidence: Measured. `code` reachable, scratch repo with no dot_config/: 'sync-baseline: line 50: .../src/dot_config/vscode-extensions.txt: No such file or directory' immediately followed by '    updated dot_config/vscode-extensions.txt' and then '==> Capturing Claude plugin manifests' -- the run continued. `code` reachable, scratch repo WITH dot_config/, tree clean before the run (porcelain empty): the run printed '==> Committing 1 file', commits 1->2, and dot_config/ afterwards holds keep.txt and vscode-extensions.txt. dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:40-50. constitution.md:130.

findings.description: The second new coupling checked for vacuity and found not vacuous, though weak. B-3's attached case is trivially green under all three per-detector mutations, because none of them touches a path the attached case reaches -- so that half of the requirement discriminates nothing. It is not vacuous, because it is coverage rather than discrimination and B-3's first half reads the case directly and requires it to assert the run commits normally; a stub assertion would be caught there, and B-2 independently requires it to drive the real script.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:121 against :64 (the three mutations, all inside the guard, which does not fire on an attached HEAD with no markers) and :114 (B-2's read). Measured: the unguarded baseline on an attached clean tree exits 0 with 'Nothing to commit', and on an attached dirty tree exits 0 with commits 1->2, in both cases untouched by any guard mutation.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: all nine cases plus the two attached cases are constructible under the authoritative-PATH harness, and the unguarded baseline exits 0 in every one of them, so every case discriminates and all three per-detector mutations have something to flip. Revision 3's decision to settle B/C by fiat ('B and C are directories, detected by existence, and `mkdir` is sufficient') resolves the r1 minor by stating the contract rather than by matching a real rebase's on-disk shape; that is a legitimate call for a constitution to make, and an existence-based detector also catches the real stopped rebase in E1, so nothing correct is excluded.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline at 298c8a6, `export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"`, dates pinned. A1 EXIT=0 1->2; A2 EXIT=0 1->1; B1 EXIT=0 1->2 (PRE_ATTACHED=yes); B2 EXIT=0 1->1; C1 EXIT=0 1->2; C2 EXIT=0 1->1; D1 EXIT=0 1->2; D2 EXIT=0 1->1; E1 PRE_ATTACHED=no PRE_STAGED=[c.txt,] EXIT=0 2->3; attached-dirty EXIT=0 1->2; attached-clean EXIT=0 1->1. constitution.md:44-58.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND on the mechanism it depends on, with one caveat already counted under the B-4 blocker. The log is written to the redirected HOME and matches the run's merged stream exactly, with no process-substitution flush race -- `exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1` at :26 does not lose trailing output on the early-exit paths this clause reads. The caveat is that V-5's clean-tree assertion is satisfied by a guard placed after the clean-tree exit whenever the harness has dirtied those cases, so V-5 is not an independent backstop for the placement requirement.
findings.evidence: Measured, 8 trials of the attached-clean case: $HOME/.local/state/dotfiles/last-sync.log byte-identical to the captured stream every time, 12 lines each. Under a harness with dirtied clean cases and a guard placed after :133, case A2's log contains 1 'Refusing' line and 0 'Nothing to commit' lines -- exactly what constitution.md:94 requires.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: every citation revision 3 added or carried, re-derived rather than diffed against the revision log. The two PATH precedents are quoted correctly and in the right polarity, B-1's regex is still byte-identical to the one lint.bats actually applies, D-2's floors all match, and the antipatterns entry the PATH requirement leans on exists.
findings.evidence: tests/apps.bats:73 = 'export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"'; tests/doctor.bats:62 = 'export PATH="$STUBS:$PATH"'. B-1's fenced pattern compared programmatically against tests/lint.bats:50 -> identical substring, True. _working-memory/antipatterns.md:41 = '2026-08-05 - Don't trust a PATH stub to isolate this repo's scripts'. Script cites re-derived: :16 set -euo pipefail; :26 exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1; :33-36 notify_fail; :66 chezmoi re-add; :87-95 the drift loop; :90 the source-path || continue; :104 the brew/jq guard; :128 cd "$SRC"; :130-133 the clean-tree exit; :153-158 the push-default rationale; :159-182 the push path; file is 182 lines. D-2 floors measured with /usr/bin/grep -c '^@test': apps 18, doctor 11, font 44, install-failures 17, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, lint 1, packages 13; `bats --count tests/` = 120; `bats tests/` green.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, including one way it could have failed a correct implementation that neither prior audit checked. This job writes its own state under .agent-guild/state/, and if that state were tracked, `git diff --name-only 298c8a6..HEAD` would carry paths outside D-1's allowlist and fail a correct worker. It is not tracked: live guild state is gitignored and only the archive is exempted, which is what the commit before the baseline arranged.
findings.evidence: .gitignore:8 '.agent-guild/state/*' and :9 '!.agent-guild/state/archive/'; `git check-ignore -v` confirms constitution.md, verdicts/ and tasks/ are all matched by line 8. Baseline commit 298c8a6; the preceding commit is 'chore(guild): let archived job state travel, keep the live state local'. constitution.md:141.

findings.description: Two isolation details the stub contract does not name. Neither is a defect today and neither changes the verdict, but both belong in a clause whose stated principle is that 'every stub is named rather than assumed.' First, redirecting HOME also strips the global git identity, so `git commit` in the scratch repo falls back to an auto-detected user@host and emits an eight-line advisory into the merged stream; harmless for V-4 because both runs get it, but a checker should either set repo-local user.name/user.email or expect the noise. Second, XDG_CONFIG_HOME survives the HOME redirect, and git reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, so the isolation B-4 buys is one file away from leaking the developer's real git config into every probe.
findings.evidence: Measured: HOME redirected, no repo-local identity, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin -> commit succeeds with 'Committer: Kendrick Arnett <karnett@That-Air.lan>' plus the 'Your name and email address were configured automatically' advisory, rc=0. XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/Users/karnett/.config is exported in this environment; ~/.config/git/config does not currently exist, so nothing leaks today. constitution.md:132.
